questions.q: What does CREATE TABLE trips USING DELTA LOCATION '...' actually do?
options: Converts the table to CSV format
Deletes the existing data at that location before creating an empty table
Creates a temporary view that disappears when the session ends
Registers "trips" as a real, persistent name in the metastore, pointing at that storage path
questions.explain: Unlike Foundations' temp views, a registered table persists for good, independent of any notebook or session.

questions.q: Why is a named table preferred for most real production tables over a bare path?
options: Chapter 4's access control grants and revokes permissions on named catalog objects, not on bare storage paths
There is no real difference; the choice is purely aesthetic
Named tables use a completely different underlying file format
Bare paths cannot be read by Spark at all
questions.explain: You can't grant someone access to "a path" — only to a real catalog object.

questions.q: What does CONVERT TO DELTA do to an existing Parquet folder?
options: Deletes the Parquet files and requires re-uploading the data
Adds a _delta_log/ in place, without rewriting the actual Parquet data files
Rewrites every data file into a completely new binary format
Only works if the folder is empty
questions.explain: This is the real migration path from "we already have Parquet" to "now it's Delta" with no full data rewrite.

questions.q: How does reading from a registered Delta table differ from Foundations' temp views (Lesson 58)?
options: Registered tables require re-reading the DataFrame every time, unlike temp views
Temp views can be queried with SQL, but registered tables cannot
A registered table persists indefinitely; a temp view existed only for the life of the SparkSession that created it
They are functionally identical in every respect
questions.explain: SELECT * FROM trips works directly for a registered table, with no spark.read call needed first, in any future session.

questions.q: What's the simplest way to create a Delta table directly from a DataFrame?
options: By calling trips.toDelta() directly
trips.write.format("delta").save(path) — the same write pattern from Lesson 14, addressed by storage path
Only through the CREATE TABLE SQL syntax; there's no DataFrame-based way
Delta tables cannot be created from a DataFrame at all
questions.explain: This works from any notebook that knows the path, with no metastore registration needed.
